chapter: Bolden and the road to New Orleans
title: Keeping a promise to stay in Laplace until twenty-one
summary: Ory kept his promise to his parents, bought his sister a house and built his own, working in a sawmill.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Meat nose, no. Yeah, a fair, pretty nose. They were having good. Wouldn't brag off everybody. It was okay. It was a definite nose and not something special. So you didn't get to play with it? No, he wouldn't let me stay. I wanted to. But you had made a promise. I made a promise to my mother and dad. I would live with my sister until I was 21. And I did. I was 21, 4, 30 in the morning and 8 o'clock I was on the train. Made it for New Orleans, I've been gone ever since. Really? Yeah. I stuck to my promise.
Did you stay in Laplace until you were 21 years old?

Yeah, and I bought my sister a home. She didn't have a home, I bought her together. In Laplace? Yeah. Called Cherokee Town, it's a village, you know, something like this. Uh-huh, uh-huh. I bought a home for what good she did for me after I got all some money.
Uh-huh. She died in that home.
She died in that. Until you were 21, what did you do in Laplace?

Well, I worked in the sawmill a while, you know. So I bought the house, I bought the lot first in there. Uh-huh. And I bought green lumber, you know. Uh-huh. Just come out from the saw and he told me if I could get a wagon to haul it from my lot, and I was dried and that I could build. And Cypress, too. Yeah. And I wanted to take a mortgage on my lot. He had so much confidence in me, he wouldn't want any mortgage, he just trust me. And I built a house.
